decisions.summary: One write page session of four questions, one check-and-apply session, then the answer on #7; no code, map or canon change.
decisions.why: Process for producing the four answers the request asks for; the no-code scope matches a research request and FR-005.

decisions.summary: Passes are leads only; every passage read on its page before citing; the Kawakami scanned notes read on page images via source-reader IMAGES=.
decisions.why: Method of verifying sources; the request asks for checked verdicts per figure ('I verify and close'), and this serves that.

decisions.summary: Where 0255-0258 give an item (relief panels, cover-shed in the Mitake repair, worship hall, copper roof, great stone torii, enshrinement cost share) the question points at the page and states its limit rather than repeating it.
decisions.why: The request says verbatim: 'Where #6's answer already covers an item ..., say so rather than repeating it.' Stating the limit adds nothing beyond saying so honestly; every such item still sits in a question (D1 table lists relief panels, cover-shed, torii, enshrinement).

decisions.summary: Each figure sits beside the same place-and-period craftsman and unskilled wage where a source gives them; where none does, the wage is stated SILENT and the nearest wage named with its class, place, unit and gap in years; a craftsman wage is never shown as unskilled.
decisions.why: The request asks for 'each figure beside the craftsman's and laborer's day wage of the same place and period'. Showing an unattested same-place wage is impossible, not merely awkward (the passes found no new wage). The fallback keeps the rule's purpose - letting gm-assistant grade each figure against labor - by naming the nearest wage with its gap, and marks the silence rather than hiding it. The bar on passing a craftsman wage off as unskilled protects the request's two-wage distinction.

decisions.summary: Wages in hand: Kumehara 1830 carpenter, Tama 1749, Edo carpenter 1804-60, Kyoto 1802-04 unskilled, Jiangsu 1769 norms.
decisions.why: An inventory of the wage sources the request's 'beside it' rule draws on; Jiangsu serves the China fallback figures only, consistent with Japan-first.

decisions.summary: I-XI N/A; XII research: physical with five boxes; XIII record checks green; XVI built as the FRs.
Four new money questions, one per request section, tagged subject=money, no drawing page, level counts-and-measurements, with setting tags countryside / countryside,city.
decisions.why: The request has four numbered questions and asks 'per question: the fragment FILE'. Tags and level are record metadata.

decisions.summary: Q1 covers kasuga and shinmei, hokora, cover-shed, pavilion and offering hall, timber, thatch and shingle, paint and lacquer, relief panels, beam-end carving, transoms (copper roof via the covered-by rule).
decisions.why: Every item of request section 1 is carried; the copper roof is carried by TC/covered-by-6 (0256) and D3's 'or the page that covers it'. The offering hall is a related silence reported, not a scope change.

decisions.summary: Q2 covers the small torii (great torii via 0257 as upper bound), lanterns, mason's day, stairway and plinth, komainu and foxes, basin, stele, gorinto, coffer.
decisions.why: Every item of section 2 including 'in stone and mason-days' is carried. 'Small torii' is not a narrowing: the great torii is still pointed at through the covered-by rule, and the builder's option is a small shrine's torii.

decisions.summary: Q3 covers mirror, gong, hanging lanterns, reliquary, offering chest and lock, lacquered chest, plus the copper floor and Qing copper ware.
decisions.why: All six request items carried; the copper floor and the China fallback are the nearest evidence for silent items, consistent with 'Japan-first'.

decisions.summary: Q4 covers night enshrinement, goryo festival, eitai kuyo, portion to a mountain temple, washing bones, calligrapher's plaque fee.
Each question gives every figure, every silence, each covered-by with its limit, each figure beside its wages; project-computed figures labeled as the project's arithmetic.
decisions.why: Matches 'the verdict per figure' and the beside-wages rule; labeling arithmetic keeps verdicts honest.

decisions.summary: implementation-check.md: one 'no code implements it - consumed by gm-assistant's money skill' line per question, with the search.
decisions.why: Carries FR-003; the consumer named is the request's own author.

decisions.summary: Comment on #7 gives each question's fragment FILE, the checked verdict per figure or the covering page, and what is still open; supersedes the interim comment.
decisions.why: Is the request's 'What the skill needs back' clause item by item; superseding the interim is what the interim comment itself promised.

decisions.summary: Page sessions, implementation check, answer, report and land by the direct route.
